commit.message:
feat(fullscreen): inline comment composer + layout polish (#4424)

* feat(fullscreen): add inline comment bar to fullscreen video feed

Adds a TikTok-style "Add comment..." pill at the bottom of
PooledFullscreenVideoFeedScreen (Explore/Search/Profile/deep-links).
Tapping focuses the field; sending dismisses the keyboard and shows
a snackbar without ever opening the full comments sheet.

The bar lives inside the Scaffold body (Column with Expanded + bar)
rather than `Scaffold.bottomNavigationBar` so it rides above the
keyboard via the default `resizeToAvoidBottomInset`. Tapping outside
the field unfocuses it, matching the DM conversation pattern.

Drive-by layout fixes the comment bar exposed on the same screen:
- Always `extendBodyBehindAppBar: true` so the video is edge-to-edge
  under the transparent app bar, matching the home feed. Removes the
  obsolete `fullscreenContainedVideoTopInset` workaround.
- Missing-dimension videos (older Vine reposts) now use `BoxFit.cover`,
  aligning with the home feed's `_FittedVideoPlayer` policy.
- Author info and action column are siblings in the same outer Stack,
  both at `bottom: 20`, so they cannot drift apart vertically and the
  gap above the bar matches the home feed.

* feat(fullscreen): fade action column top when keyboard is up

When the inline comment composer pulls the keyboard up, Scaffold
shrinks the body and the action column slides toward the transparent
AppBar — the Like and Reply icons land underneath the back / title /
More buttons. KeyboardAwareTopFade wraps the column in a ShaderMask
(BlendMode.dstIn, transparent through the top 20 %, linear fade to
opaque at the bottom) so the overlap is invisible. Pass-through when
no keyboard is visible to avoid the save-layer cost on the steady
feed.

Listening for the inset has to go through WidgetsBindingObserver:
Scaffold's resizeToAvoidBottomInset strips viewInsets.bottom from
the body's MediaQuery, and View.of(context) is not reactive to
inset changes. Also drops the stale MediaQueryData.fromView wrap
in the fullscreen item builder — it was a snapshot that broke live
viewInsets propagation to anything below it.

* feat(fullscreen): animate the action-column fade in parallel with the keyboard

Triggering the fade off `viewInsets.bottom == 0` ran it sequentially
after the keyboard had finished sliding away. Drive it off the
direction of viewInsets.bottom instead: on iOS and Android the
platform animates the inset over the OS keyboard curve and Flutter
fires didChangeMetrics each frame, so the first decrease after a
non-zero value is the start of the hide animation. Snap the
ShaderMask on as soon as the inset starts rising from 0; reverse
the 100 ms fade as soon as it starts dropping again. The column
fade now runs in parallel with the platform keyboard slide rather
than chasing its tail.

This also keeps the right semantics on macOS / desktop where a
TextField can take focus by click without the platform keyboard
ever appearing — viewInsets.bottom stays at 0 throughout, so the
mask never activates.

* feat(fullscreen): round the feed bottom and tint the scaffold to match the bar

Wrap the feed in NavRoundedShell when the inline comment bar is on
screen, mirroring the home feed composition at video_feed_page.dart.
The shell's outer ColoredBox paints VineTheme.navGreen, which is the
same Color(0xFF00150D) token the bar uses as VineTheme.surfaceBackground
— so the 30 px rounded-corner cutouts at the bottom of the video
seam continuously into the bar instead of revealing black.

Also flip the Scaffold backgroundColor from VineTheme.backgroundColor
(black) to VineTheme.surfaceBackground so any sliver of Scaffold
peeking through (device curved-corner cutouts at the bar's bottom
edges, the safe-area strip below the keyboard) is the same green as
the bar, not black.

* feat(fullscreen): restyle the inline comment send button to match Figma

Match Figma node 2018:29838 ("primary"). The button is a 48 × 48
component with 20 radius / 32 icon / 8 padding at native scale, and
the composition at 14368:75902 scales it into a 40 px slot at
40 / 48 = 0.833× — radius becomes 16.667, icon becomes 26.667. The
20 / 48 = 41.7 % radius ratio is a heavily rounded rectangle, not a
circle (a circle would need 50 %). The icon is the Phosphor `ArrowUp`
bold-fill shape, swapped from Material `Icons.arrow_upward` to the
divine_ui `DivineIcon` so the geometry matches. Two stacked sub-pixel
drop shadows (`shadow-10` = #0000001A) give a faint elevation cue.

Icon color flipped from white to `VineTheme.onPrimaryButton`
(`#003824`) — the Figma vector's `fill="var(--fill-0, #003824)"`
makes it explicit, and the rendered Figma asset confirms dark
green-on-green, the M3 contrast convention for `primary/on-primary`.

* feat(fullscreen): match Figma app bar title size and leading gap

The fullscreen feed's app bar was rendering the title at
[VineTheme.titleLargeFont] (22 / 28 / 0) and leaving the default
80 px leading slot, which put 24 px between the back button's
right edge and the title text. Figma node 17352:104146 uses the
`title/medium` token (Bricolage Grotesque 800 16 / 24 / 0.15) and
a tighter gap. Switch the title style to `titleMediumFont` and
shrink `leadingWidth` to 68 so the gap becomes 12 px (68 − 8 − 48).

* feat(divine_ui): let DiVineAppBar expand the leading hit area to the full slot

Adds an opt-in `expandLeadingHitArea: bool = false` on
[DiVineAppBar] (forwarded to [DiVineAppBarLeading] as
`expandHitArea`). When set, the back / menu / leading button still
renders at its configured size and position, but the tap target
stretches to the full leading slot. Inside `_LeadingIconButton` the
visible button gets wrapped in `GestureDetector(behavior: opaque) →
AbsorbPointer(child: visibleButton)` — the inner
[DiVineAppBarIconButton] keeps its semantics for screen readers
while [AbsorbPointer] stops it from receiving pointer events, so
taps don't double-fire and the outer [GestureDetector] is the
single hit-test surface.

Opt the fullscreen feed in: the back button sits over playing
video where the smaller 48 × 48 icon button is easy to miss, so a
72 × 72 (leading-slot-sized) tap target is a meaningful UX win.

Also drop the inner `Padding(end: 4)` wrapper around the
trailing [FeedSettingsMenu] so the trailing inset matches the
leading: both buttons now sit 12 px from their respective screen
edges (visible-icon edges at 20 px and 20 / 24 px depending on icon
size). New tests at `divine_app_bar_test.dart` cover both the
opted-in expansion and the unchanged default behavior.

* feat(fullscreen): scrim the top of the video so the transparent app bar reads

The transparent app bar over the fullscreen feed was hard to read
over light video frames — the bottom of the screen already had a
darkening LinearGradient inside [VideoOverlayActions], but the top
had none.

Add a symmetric `showTopGradient: bool = false` flag to
[VideoOverlayActions]. When true, a [Positioned] at `top: 0`
renders a `LinearGradient` from `VineTheme.backgroundColor` at 35 %
alpha down to fully transparent, sized to the top 20 % of the
screen, wrapped in [IgnorePointer] so it doesn't claim any gestures.
The gradient lives inside the Scaffold body's Stack so Scaffold's
own slot ordering paints the app bar above it — meaning the app
bar's back / title / More tap targets remain on top in both paint
and hit-test order.

Opt the two fullscreen `VideoOverlayActions` instances in
[_PooledFullscreenItem] and [_PooledFullscreenItemContent] into
the new scrim. Home feed and editor / preview surfaces keep the
default `false`.

* feat(fullscreen): grow the inline comment composer 1–5 lines like the bottom sheet

The inline composer bar's TextField was fixed to a single line —
long comments got clipped horizontally. Mirror the comments-sheet
`CommentInput` so the inline variant behaves identically:

- `keyboardType: TextInputType.multiline`, `minLines: 1`,
  `maxLines: 5` on the field — long comments wrap up to five lines
  and scroll past that.
- Drop the fixed `SizedBox(height: 72)` wrapper and the
  `InlineCommentComposerBar.contentHeight` constant (only used
  internally). The pill now has `ConstrainedBox(minHeight: 48)` so
  it grows with the text field and the surrounding Column resizes
  to match.
- Row inside the pill uses `crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.end`
  so the send button stays anchored to the pill's bottom-right
  corner while the field grows. `_SendButton` got `bottom: 4`
  padding so it sits 4 px above the pill's bottom edge, matching
  the comments-sheet button geometry.
- Outer pill spacing switched from `symmetric(horizontal: 16,
  vertical: 12)` to `EdgeInsetsDirectional.fromSTEB(16, 16, 16, 8)`
  — same `LTRB(16, 16, 16, 8)` the comments-sheet uses around its
  pill — and the field's internal padding picked up the
  `top: 14, bottom: 14` from there too, so single-line vertical
  rhythm matches exactly.

New test locks in `minLines: 1`, `maxLines: 5`, and
`keyboardType: multiline` so the multi-line contract is regressionproof.

* feat(fullscreen): stop tap-outside-to-dismiss from toggling video playback

Tapping the video while the inline comment composer's keyboard is
open used to both (a) fire the TextField's onTapOutside (dismiss
the keyboard — intended) and (b) reach the video's play / pause
recognizer underneath (toggle playback — unintended).

Add a `VideoTapShield` that wraps the feed area and, while a text
input has primary focus, overlays a transparent
`GestureDetector(behavior: opaque)`. The shield claims the tap in
the gesture arena so the video recognizer never sees it. Keyboard
dismissal still happens because `TextField.onTapOutside` is wired
through `TapRegion` / `TapRegionSurface`, which reads pointer
events at the surface level — *independent* of the gesture arena,
so the claim above does not suppress the unfocus callback.

Focus is detected the same way [KeyboardAwareTopFade] does it:
[FocusManager.addListener] + `findAncestorWidgetOfExactType<EditableText>`
on the primary-focus node. That keeps macOS / desktop behaving
right (a clicked TextField with no software keyboard never triggers
the shield).

Tests at video_tap_shield_test.dart lock in all three transitions:
no-focus → child receives tap; focus → child does NOT receive tap;
focus-then-unfocus → child receives tap again.

* feat(fullscreen): keep the keyboard up while the user interacts with the app bar

Tapping the More button / X button / playback toggles while the
inline composer's keyboard was up dismissed the keyboard via
`TextField.onTapOutside`, forcing the user to refocus and retype.

Two changes:

* The fullscreen feed wraps its [DiVineAppBar] in a
  `PreferredSize → TextFieldTapRegion` so taps anywhere on the AppBar
  (back button, title, More trigger) count as inside the focused
  TextField's tap-region group. [TapRegion] is independent of the
  gesture arena, so each AppBar control still fires its own
  `onTap` — only the unfocus side-effect is suppressed.
* The [_FeedSettingsOverlay] in [FeedSettingsMenu] wraps its
  *entire* overlay (backdrop catcher + pill) in
  `TextFieldTapRegion`, not just the pill. The previous "pill-only"
  scope missed the case where the popover's full-screen dismiss
  catcher overlays the X button in the app bar — tapping there
  closed the popover but also fired the composer's onTapOutside.
  Wrapping the whole overlay keeps the popover and the keyboard
  fully independent: closing the popover (via X or backdrop) no
  longer touches the keyboard, and toggling playback controls
  doesn't either.

* fix(fullscreen): stop stretching 1 × 1 / landscape videos, center them on green

Three things were going wrong for contain-fit videos on the
fullscreen feed:

* The isPortrait heuristic short-circuited on missing dimensions and
  treated classic 1 × 1 Vine reposts as portrait, applying
  `BoxFit.cover` and vertically stretching the square frame. Drop
  the short-circuit so isPortrait reflects only what `VideoEvent`
  actually claims (`height > width`); 1 × 1 / landscape / unknown
  all fall to `BoxFit.contain`.
* `fullscreenVideoMediaAlignment` used `Alignment.topCenter` for
  contain-fit videos, jamming the 1 × 1 against the AppBar. Always
  return `Alignment.center` so square and landscape sources sit in
  the middle of the viewport with symmetric bands above and below.
* `_MaybeRoundFeedBottom` overrode [NavRoundedShell.innerColor] to
  [VineTheme.backgroundColor] (`#000000`), which made the letterbox
  bands render black. Drop the override and let the shell use its
  default [VineTheme.surfaceBackground] (`#00150D` — the same green
  the comment bar paints), so the bands now read as a continuous
  green canvas seaming into the bar.

Updated the alignment test to assert `Alignment.center` for the
non-portrait case and refreshed the related Scaffold comment that
referenced the now-removed "treat missing dimensions as portrait"
hack.

* feat(fullscreen): paint the letterbox canvas with cardBackground

The fullscreen feed's Scaffold and the inner of [_MaybeRoundFeedBottom]
were briefly set to [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh] (`#000A06`) so the
canvas around 1 × 1 / landscape / dimensions-less contain-fit videos
would read as a separate surface from the comment bar. The hex sits at
RGB `(0, 10, 6)`, which is below the perceptual threshold on a phone
screen — visually identical to pure black, defeating the point.

Switch both to [VineTheme.cardBackground] (`#1A1A1A`) — the same
neutral dark grey the Messages inbox scaffold uses at
[inbox_view.dart:498]. That's clearly off-black and reads as a distinct
surface against the comment bar's `#00150D` green, matching the user's
intent.

* feat(fullscreen): blurred-thumbnail backdrop behind contain-fit videos

Letterbox bands for 1 × 1 / landscape / dimensions-less videos used
to render as a flat dark surface — even the surface colour changes
from earlier commits were silently dropped because
[_PooledFullscreenItemContent] wraps [PooledVideoPlayer] in
`ColoredBox(color: VineTheme.backgroundColor)` (`#000000`), which
overpaints the Scaffold and [NavRoundedShell] surfaces and is what
actually shows through the letterbox.

Three changes:

* Flip that overpaint from [VineTheme.backgroundColor] to
  [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh] (`#000A06`), the canvas the
  Scaffold and [_MaybeRoundFeedBottom] are already painted with —
  brings all three surfaces into agreement instead of fighting each
  other.
* Wrap the [PooledVideoPlayer] in a [Stack] and, for non-portrait
  videos with a thumbnail, paint a [_BlurredVideoBackdrop] behind
  it. The backdrop is the video's poster thumbnail with `BoxFit.cover`,
  blurred via [ImageFiltered] / `ui.ImageFilter.blur(30, 30)` and
  painted at 50 % alpha through [Image.opacity] (cheaper than an
  [Opacity] wrapper — blends per-pixel during paint instead of
  forcing a full-screen save-layer). Cost is one image decode + one
  GPU blur pass, both cached. Portrait videos cover the whole
  viewport so the backdrop is gated off for them.
* Restore the outer Scaffold + [_MaybeRoundFeedBottom] to
  [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh] after the [VineTheme.cardBackground]
  detour, so the fallback when the thumbnail fails to load matches
  the rest of the canvas.

Contain-fit videos now sit in a diffused colour cloud derived from
their own first frame — the static-blurhash treatment we agreed on
earlier — instead of a flat dark band.

* fix(fullscreen): restore green-behind-keyboard and use actual video aspect

Two regressions from the recent blur-backdrop work:

* The Scaffold backgroundColor briefly went to
  [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh] alongside the video item, which
  meant the strip below the soft keyboard (and the device's curved
  corner cutouts at the bottom edges) stopped reading as green. The
  Scaffold needs to stay [VineTheme.surfaceBackground] (`#00150D`) so
  it continues the comment bar's surface around the keyboard; the
  near-black canvas around the video lives on the video item's own
  ColoredBox + the NavRoundedShell inner. Revert the Scaffold only.

* Portrait videos with missing / inaccurate dimensions metadata
  stopped filling the screen — the previous formula was
  metadata-only (`video.isPortrait`) so a portrait whose VideoEvent
  lacked dimensions fell to [BoxFit.contain] and letterboxed. Make
  [_FittedVideoPlayer] reactive to [VideoController.rect] (a
  `ValueNotifier<Rect?>` `media_kit` populates with the live
  texture rect once the platform reports decoded dimensions): now
  the BoxFit decision tracks the *actual* video aspect — 1 × 1
  contain, portrait cover, landscape contain — and the metadata
  hint is only used as a fallback while `rect` is still null.

* fix(fullscreen): pin the inline comment pill to Figma's 48 px single-line height

The TextField inside the composer pill had `top: 14, bottom: 14`
vertical padding (inherited verbatim from the comments-sheet
composer), so single-line height worked out to `14 + 24 + 14 = 52`
px — 4 px taller than Figma node 15222:192139 specifies. Drop the
padding to `top: 12, bottom: 12` so single-line is exactly
`12 + 24 + 12 = 48` px. Multi-line growth via `minLines: 1,
maxLines: 5` still works (2 lines → 72, 3 lines → 96, …) and the
send button stays anchored to the bottom of the pill via
`CrossAxisAlignment.end`.

* chore(l10n): allow-list the inline comment composer keys as untranslated debt

Five keys added on this branch for the new fullscreen inline comment
composer ship in English but haven't been translated yet. Following
the convention established by the surrounding entries (see DM
hints, badges, people-lists, etc. in `_knownUntranslatedDebt`),
add them to the debt set with a comment naming the feature so a
future translation pass can pick them up. Non-English locales fall
back to the English source until then.

* docs(feed): refresh FeedSettingsMenu docstring to cover both call sites

The class docstring described FeedSettingsMenu as living only on the
home feed's top bar — accurate when the widget was introduced, stale
now that the fullscreen video screen also embeds it as a
`customActions` entry on its DiVineAppBar. Reword to name both
surfaces so future readers don't assume the home feed is the only
caller.

* docs(fullscreen): refresh InlineCommentComposerBar docstring after layout pivot

The class docstring still described the bar as living in
`Scaffold.bottomNavigationBar` with a fixed 72 px content height —
both stale. The bar now lives inside the Scaffold body so the
keyboard can push it up rather than stranding it below the keyboard,
and its height grows with the TextField's 1–5-line range instead of
being pinned to 72 px. Reword to match.

* fix(fullscreen): restore the inline composer's draft on publish failure

`_handleSubmit` cleared the field optimistically before knowing the
publish result. On the cubit's `failure` path that left the user
staring at an empty pill and a "couldn't post" snackbar — their
typed comment was gone for good. Regression vs the comments-sheet
flow, where [CommentsBloc] rolls `mainInputText` back to
`previousMain` on rollback at [comments_bloc.dart:414].

Mirror that behavior locally: snapshot the field's text into a new
`_pendingDraft` at submit-time, then restore it from the
[BlocListener] when the cubit emits `failure`. Guard the restore on
`controller.text.isEmpty` so we don't clobber any text the user has
already started typing after the optimistic clear. Keep the cubit
itself minimal (status-only) per its docstring's stated design —
the draft is widget-local, just like the controller.

Two new widget tests pin the contract: failure after an optimistic
clear restores the draft + re-shows the send button; failure that
lands after the user has started a new draft preserves the new
text and drops the stale one.

Addresses PR #4424 review comment 3253170130.

* docs(fullscreen): correct two token-naming errors in screen-file comments

Two inline comments referenced the wrong tokens for the colors they
were describing:

* [fullscreenVideoMediaAlignment] claimed contain-fit bands were
  filled with [VineTheme.surfaceBackground]. The canvas around
  contain-fit videos in this file is [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh]
  (set by both [_MaybeRoundFeedBottom]'s [NavRoundedShell] and
  [_PooledFullscreenItemContent]'s `ColoredBox`). Tightened the
  docstring to explain only the alignment decision rather than
  trying to document the painting stack across two other widgets.

* The body comment introducing [_MaybeRoundFeedBottom] claimed the
  rounded corner reveal and the comment bar paint the same token.
  Actually the corners reveal [VineTheme.navGreen] (the outer of
  [NavRoundedShell]) and the bar paints
  [VineTheme.surfaceBackground]. They happen to share the hex
  `#00150D`, which is why the seam reads as continuous — but
  "same hex" is not "same token", and the comment now says so
  explicitly so a future retune of one token doesn't silently
  invalidate the rationale.

Addresses PR #4424 review comments 3253170132 and 3253170133.

* docs(fullscreen): correct surfaceContainerHigh hex and outer-color token in _MaybeRoundFeedBottom

The body comment introducing the [NavRoundedShell] in
[_MaybeRoundFeedBottom] had three drift items:

* Claimed [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh] is `#1A1A1A`. The token
  is `#000A06` (see vine_theme.dart). `#1A1A1A` is
  [VineTheme.cardBackground] — a different token.
* Claimed surfaceContainerHigh is "the same neutral dark grey the
  Messages inbox uses." The Messages inbox uses cardBackground,
  not surfaceContainerHigh. The Messages-inbox association is
  residue from an earlier iteration where this code briefly used
  cardBackground; the comment was never updated when the token
  changed.
* Attributed the shell's outer color to [VineTheme.surfaceBackground]
  — same conflation as the line-870 comment fixed in a8071dd63.
  [NavRoundedShell]'s outer is [VineTheme.navGreen]; it shares its
  hex with surfaceBackground, which is what actually makes the
  seam continuous.

Corrected all three and tightened the seam claim so it depends on
the shared hex (an observable fact today) rather than on the two
tokens being the same (which they aren't).

Addresses PR #4424 review comment 3253170135.

shrinks the body and the action column slides toward the transparent
AppBar — the Like and Reply icons land underneath the back / title /
More buttons. KeyboardAwareTopFade wraps the column in a ShaderMask
(BlendMode.dstIn, transparent through the top 20 %, linear fade to
opaque at the bottom) so the overlap is invisible. Pass-through when
no keyboard is visible to avoid the save-layer cost on the steady
feed.

Listening for the inset has to go through WidgetsBindingObserver:
Scaffold's resizeToAvoidBottomInset strips viewInsets.bottom from
the body's MediaQuery, and View.of(context) is not reactive to
inset changes. Also drops the stale MediaQueryData.fromView wrap
in the fullscreen item builder — it was a snapshot that broke live
viewInsets propagation to anything below it.

* feat(fullscreen): animate the action-column fade in parallel with the keyboard

Triggering the fade off `viewInsets.bottom == 0` ran it sequentially
after the keyboard had finished sliding away. Drive it off the
direction of viewInsets.bottom instead: on iOS and Android the
platform animates the inset over the OS keyboard curve and Flutter
fires didChangeMetrics each frame, so the first decrease after a
non-zero value is the start of the hide animation. Snap the
ShaderMask on as soon as the inset starts rising from 0; reverse
the 100 ms fade as soon as it starts dropping again. The column
fade now runs in parallel with the platform keyboard slide rather
than chasing its tail.

This also keeps the right semantics on macOS / desktop where a
TextField can take focus by click without the platform keyboard
ever appearing — viewInsets.bottom stays at 0 throughout, so the
mask never activates.

* feat(fullscreen): round the feed bottom and tint the scaffold to match the bar

Wrap the feed in NavRoundedShell when the inline comment bar is on
screen, mirroring the home feed composition at video_feed_page.dart.
The shell's outer ColoredBox paints VineTheme.navGreen, which is the
same Color(0xFF00150D) token the bar uses as VineTheme.surfaceBackground
— so the 30 px rounded-corner cutouts at the bottom of the video
seam continuously into the bar instead of revealing black.

Also flip the Scaffold backgroundColor from VineTheme.backgroundColor
(black) to VineTheme.surfaceBackground so any sliver of Scaffold
peeking through (device curved-corner cutouts at the bar's bottom
edges, the safe-area strip below the keyboard) is the same green as
the bar, not black.

* feat(fullscreen): restyle the inline comment send button to match Figma

Match Figma node 2018:29838 ("primary"). The button is a 48 × 48
component with 20 radius / 32 icon / 8 padding at native scale, and
the composition at 14368:75902 scales it into a 40 px slot at
40 / 48 = 0.833× — radius becomes 16.667, icon becomes 26.667. The
20 / 48 = 41.7 % radius ratio is a heavily rounded rectangle, not a
circle (a circle would need 50 %). The icon is the Phosphor `ArrowUp`
bold-fill shape, swapped from Material `Icons.arrow_upward` to the
divine_ui `DivineIcon` so the geometry matches. Two stacked sub-pixel
drop shadows (`shadow-10` = #0000001A) give a faint elevation cue.

Icon color flipped from white to `VineTheme.onPrimaryButton`
(`#003824`) — the Figma vector's `fill="var(--fill-0, #003824)"`
makes it explicit, and the rendered Figma asset confirms dark
green-on-green, the M3 contrast convention for `primary/on-primary`.

* feat(fullscreen): match Figma app bar title size and leading gap

The fullscreen feed's app bar was rendering the title at
[VineTheme.titleLargeFont] (22 / 28 / 0) and leaving the default
80 px leading slot, which put 24 px between the back button's
right edge and the title text. Figma node 17352:104146 uses the
`title/medium` token (Bricolage Grotesque 800 16 / 24 / 0.15) and
a tighter gap. Switch the title style to `titleMediumFont` and
shrink `leadingWidth` to 68 so the gap becomes 12 px (68 − 8 − 48).

* feat(divine_ui): let DiVineAppBar expand the leading hit area to the full slot

Adds an opt-in `expandLeadingHitArea: bool = false` on
[DiVineAppBar] (forwarded to [DiVineAppBarLeading] as
`expandHitArea`). When set, the back / menu / leading button still
renders at its configured size and position, but the tap target
stretches to the full leading slot. Inside `_LeadingIconButton` the
visible button gets wrapped in `GestureDetector(behavior: opaque) →
AbsorbPointer(child: visibleButton)` — the inner
[DiVineAppBarIconButton] keeps its semantics for screen readers
while [AbsorbPointer] stops it from receiving pointer events, so
taps don't double-fire and the outer [GestureDetector] is the
single hit-test surface.

Opt the fullscreen feed in: the back button sits over playing
video where the smaller 48 × 48 icon button is easy to miss, so a
72 × 72 (leading-slot-sized) tap target is a meaningful UX win.

Also drop the inner `Padding(end: 4)` wrapper around the
trailing [FeedSettingsMenu] so the trailing inset matches the
leading: both buttons now sit 12 px from their respective screen
edges (visible-icon edges at 20 px and 20 / 24 px depending on icon
size). New tests at `divine_app_bar_test.dart` cover both the
opted-in expansion and the unchanged default behavior.

* feat(fullscreen): scrim the top of the video so the transparent app bar reads

The transparent app bar over the fullscreen feed was hard to read
over light video frames — the bottom of the screen already had a
darkening LinearGradient inside [VideoOverlayActions], but the top
had none.

Add a symmetric `showTopGradient: bool = false` flag to
[VideoOverlayActions]. When true, a [Positioned] at `top: 0`
renders a `LinearGradient` from `VineTheme.backgroundColor` at 35 %
alpha down to fully transparent, sized to the top 20 % of the
screen, wrapped in [IgnorePointer] so it doesn't claim any gestures.
The gradient lives inside the Scaffold body's Stack so Scaffold's
own slot ordering paints the app bar above it — meaning the app
bar's back / title / More tap targets remain on top in both paint
and hit-test order.

Opt the two fullscreen `VideoOverlayActions` instances in
[_PooledFullscreenItem] and [_PooledFullscreenItemContent] into
the new scrim. Home feed and editor / preview surfaces keep the
default `false`.

* feat(fullscreen): grow the inline comment composer 1–5 lines like the bottom sheet

The inline composer bar's TextField was fixed to a single line —
long comments got clipped horizontally. Mirror the comments-sheet
`CommentInput` so the inline variant behaves identically:

- `keyboardType: TextInputType.multiline`, `minLines: 1`,
  `maxLines: 5` on the field — long comments wrap up to five lines
  and scroll past that.
- Drop the fixed `SizedBox(height: 72)` wrapper and the
  `InlineCommentComposerBar.contentHeight` constant (only used
  internally). The pill now has `ConstrainedBox(minHeight: 48)` so
  it grows with the text field and the surrounding Column resizes
  to match.
- Row inside the pill uses `crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.end`
  so the send button stays anchored to the pill's bottom-right
  corner while the field grows. `_SendButton` got `bottom: 4`
  padding so it sits 4 px above the pill's bottom edge, matching
  the comments-sheet button geometry.
- Outer pill spacing switched from `symmetric(horizontal: 16,
  vertical: 12)` to `EdgeInsetsDirectional.fromSTEB(16, 16, 16, 8)`
  — same `LTRB(16, 16, 16, 8)` the comments-sheet uses around its
  pill — and the field's internal padding picked up the
  `top: 14, bottom: 14` from there too, so single-line vertical
  rhythm matches exactly.

New test locks in `minLines: 1`, `maxLines: 5`, and
`keyboardType: multiline` so the multi-line contract is regressionproof.

* feat(fullscreen): stop tap-outside-to-dismiss from toggling video playback

Tapping the video while the inline comment composer's keyboard is
open used to both (a) fire the TextField's onTapOutside (dismiss
the keyboard — intended) and (b) reach the video's play / pause
recognizer underneath (toggle playback — unintended).

Add a `VideoTapShield` that wraps the feed area and, while a text
input has primary focus, overlays a transparent
`GestureDetector(behavior: opaque)`. The shield claims the tap in
the gesture arena so the video recognizer never sees it. Keyboard
dismissal still happens because `TextField.onTapOutside` is wired
through `TapRegion` / `TapRegionSurface`, which reads pointer
events at the surface level — *independent* of the gesture arena,
so the claim above does not suppress the unfocus callback.

Focus is detected the same way [KeyboardAwareTopFade] does it:
[FocusManager.addListener] + `findAncestorWidgetOfExactType<EditableText>`
on the primary-focus node. That keeps macOS / desktop behaving
right (a clicked TextField with no software keyboard never triggers
the shield).

Tests at video_tap_shield_test.dart lock in all three transitions:
no-focus → child receives tap; focus → child does NOT receive tap;
focus-then-unfocus → child receives tap again.

* feat(fullscreen): keep the keyboard up while the user interacts with the app bar

Tapping the More button / X button / playback toggles while the
inline composer's keyboard was up dismissed the keyboard via
`TextField.onTapOutside`, forcing the user to refocus and retype.

Two changes:

* The fullscreen feed wraps its [DiVineAppBar] in a
  `PreferredSize → TextFieldTapRegion` so taps anywhere on the AppBar
  (back button, title, More trigger) count as inside the focused
  TextField's tap-region group. [TapRegion] is independent of the
  gesture arena, so each AppBar control still fires its own
  `onTap` — only the unfocus side-effect is suppressed.
* The [_FeedSettingsOverlay] in [FeedSettingsMenu] wraps its
  *entire* overlay (backdrop catcher + pill) in
  `TextFieldTapRegion`, not just the pill. The previous "pill-only"
  scope missed the case where the popover's full-screen dismiss
  catcher overlays the X button in the app bar — tapping there
  closed the popover but also fired the composer's onTapOutside.
  Wrapping the whole overlay keeps the popover and the keyboard
  fully independent: closing the popover (via X or backdrop) no
  longer touches the keyboard, and toggling playback controls
  doesn't either.

* fix(fullscreen): stop stretching 1 × 1 / landscape videos, center them on green

Three things were going wrong for contain-fit videos on the
fullscreen feed:

* The isPortrait heuristic short-circuited on missing dimensions and
  treated classic 1 × 1 Vine reposts as portrait, applying
  `BoxFit.cover` and vertically stretching the square frame. Drop
  the short-circuit so isPortrait reflects only what `VideoEvent`
  actually claims (`height > width`); 1 × 1 / landscape / unknown
  all fall to `BoxFit.contain`.
* `fullscreenVideoMediaAlignment` used `Alignment.topCenter` for
  contain-fit videos, jamming the 1 × 1 against the AppBar. Always
  return `Alignment.center` so square and landscape sources sit in
  the middle of the viewport with symmetric bands above and below.
* `_MaybeRoundFeedBottom` overrode [NavRoundedShell.innerColor] to
  [VineTheme.backgroundColor] (`#000000`), which made the letterbox
  bands render black. Drop the override and let the shell use its
  default [VineTheme.surfaceBackground] (`#00150D` — the same green
  the comment bar paints), so the bands now read as a continuous
  green canvas seaming into the bar.

Updated the alignment test to assert `Alignment.center` for the
non-portrait case and refreshed the related Scaffold comment that
referenced the now-removed "treat missing dimensions as portrait"
hack.

* feat(fullscreen): paint the letterbox canvas with cardBackground

The fullscreen feed's Scaffold and the inner of [_MaybeRoundFeedBottom]
were briefly set to [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh] (`#000A06`) so the
canvas around 1 × 1 / landscape / dimensions-less contain-fit videos
would read as a separate surface from the comment bar. The hex sits at
RGB `(0, 10, 6)`, which is below the perceptual threshold on a phone
screen — visually identical to pure black, defeating the point.

Switch both to [VineTheme.cardBackground] (`#1A1A1A`) — the same
neutral dark grey the Messages inbox scaffold uses at
[inbox_view.dart:498]. That's clearly off-black and reads as a distinct
surface against the comment bar's `#00150D` green, matching the user's
intent.

* feat(fullscreen): blurred-thumbnail backdrop behind contain-fit videos

Letterbox bands for 1 × 1 / landscape / dimensions-less videos used
to render as a flat dark surface — even the surface colour changes
from earlier commits were silently dropped because
[_PooledFullscreenItemContent] wraps [PooledVideoPlayer] in
`ColoredBox(color: VineTheme.backgroundColor)` (`#000000`), which
overpaints the Scaffold and [NavRoundedShell] surfaces and is what
actually shows through the letterbox.

Three changes:

* Flip that overpaint from [VineTheme.backgroundColor] to
  [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh] (`#000A06`), the canvas the
  Scaffold and [_MaybeRoundFeedBottom] are already painted with —
  brings all three surfaces into agreement instead of fighting each
  other.
* Wrap the [PooledVideoPlayer] in a [Stack] and, for non-portrait
  videos with a thumbnail, paint a [_BlurredVideoBackdrop] behind
  it. The backdrop is the video's poster thumbnail with `BoxFit.cover`,
  blurred via [ImageFiltered] / `ui.ImageFilter.blur(30, 30)` and
  painted at 50 % alpha through [Image.opacity] (cheaper than an
  [Opacity] wrapper — blends per-pixel during paint instead of
  forcing a full-screen save-layer). Cost is one image decode + one
  GPU blur pass, both cached. Portrait videos cover the whole
  viewport so the backdrop is gated off for them.
* Restore the outer Scaffold + [_MaybeRoundFeedBottom] to
  [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh] after the [VineTheme.cardBackground]
  detour, so the fallback when the thumbnail fails to load matches
  the rest of the canvas.

Contain-fit videos now sit in a diffused colour cloud derived from
their own first frame — the static-blurhash treatment we agreed on
earlier — instead of a flat dark band.

* fix(fullscreen): restore green-behind-keyboard and use actual video aspect

Two regressions from the recent blur-backdrop work:

* The Scaffold backgroundColor briefly went to
  [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh] alongside the video item, which
  meant the strip below the soft keyboard (and the device's curved
  corner cutouts at the bottom edges) stopped reading as green. The
  Scaffold needs to stay [VineTheme.surfaceBackground] (`#00150D`) so
  it continues the comment bar's surface around the keyboard; the
  near-black canvas around the video lives on the video item's own
  ColoredBox + the NavRoundedShell inner. Revert the Scaffold only.

* Portrait videos with missing / inaccurate dimensions metadata
  stopped filling the screen — the previous formula was
  metadata-only (`video.isPortrait`) so a portrait whose VideoEvent
  lacked dimensions fell to [BoxFit.contain] and letterboxed. Make
  [_FittedVideoPlayer] reactive to [VideoController.rect] (a
  `ValueNotifier<Rect?>` `media_kit` populates with the live
  texture rect once the platform reports decoded dimensions): now
  the BoxFit decision tracks the *actual* video aspect — 1 × 1
  contain, portrait cover, landscape contain — and the metadata
  hint is only used as a fallback while `rect` is still null.

* fix(fullscreen): pin the inline comment pill to Figma's 48 px single-line height

The TextField inside the composer pill had `top: 14, bottom: 14`
vertical padding (inherited verbatim from the comments-sheet
composer), so single-line height worked out to `14 + 24 + 14 = 52`
px — 4 px taller than Figma node 15222:192139 specifies. Drop the
padding to `top: 12, bottom: 12` so single-line is exactly
`12 + 24 + 12 = 48` px. Multi-line growth via `minLines: 1,
maxLines: 5` still works (2 lines → 72, 3 lines → 96, …) and the
send button stays anchored to the bottom of the pill via
`CrossAxisAlignment.end`.

* chore(l10n): allow-list the inline comment composer keys as untranslated debt

Five keys added on this branch for the new fullscreen inline comment
composer ship in English but haven't been translated yet. Following
the convention established by the surrounding entries (see DM
hints, badges, people-lists, etc. in `_knownUntranslatedDebt`),
add them to the debt set with a comment naming the feature so a
future translation pass can pick them up. Non-English locales fall
back to the English source until then.

* docs(feed): refresh FeedSettingsMenu docstring to cover both call sites

The class docstring described FeedSettingsMenu as living only on the
home feed's top bar — accurate when the widget was introduced, stale
now that the fullscreen video screen also embeds it as a
`customActions` entry on its DiVineAppBar. Reword to name both
surfaces so future readers don't assume the home feed is the only
caller.

* docs(fullscreen): refresh InlineCommentComposerBar docstring after layout pivot

The class docstring still described the bar as living in
`Scaffold.bottomNavigationBar` with a fixed 72 px content height —
both stale. The bar now lives inside the Scaffold body so the
keyboard can push it up rather than stranding it below the keyboard,
and its height grows with the TextField's 1–5-line range instead of
being pinned to 72 px. Reword to match.

* fix(fullscreen): restore the inline composer's draft on publish failure

`_handleSubmit` cleared the field optimistically before knowing the
publish result. On the cubit's `failure` path that left the user
staring at an empty pill and a "couldn't post" snackbar — their
typed comment was gone for good. Regression vs the comments-sheet
flow, where [CommentsBloc] rolls `mainInputText` back to
`previousMain` on rollback at [comments_bloc.dart:414].

Mirror that behavior locally: snapshot the field's text into a new
`_pendingDraft` at submit-time, then restore it from the
[BlocListener] when the cubit emits `failure`. Guard the restore on
`controller.text.isEmpty` so we don't clobber any text the user has
already started typing after the optimistic clear. Keep the cubit
itself minimal (status-only) per its docstring's stated design —
the draft is widget-local, just like the controller.

Two new widget tests pin the contract: failure after an optimistic
clear restores the draft + re-shows the send button; failure that
lands after the user has started a new draft preserves the new
text and drops the stale one.

Addresses PR #4424 review comment 3253170130.

* docs(fullscreen): correct two token-naming errors in screen-file comments

Two inline comments referenced the wrong tokens for the colors they
were describing:

* [fullscreenVideoMediaAlignment] claimed contain-fit bands were
  filled with [VineTheme.surfaceBackground]. The canvas around
  contain-fit videos in this file is [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh]
  (set by both [_MaybeRoundFeedBottom]'s [NavRoundedShell] and
  [_PooledFullscreenItemContent]'s `ColoredBox`). Tightened the
  docstring to explain only the alignment decision rather than
  trying to document the painting stack across two other widgets.

* The body comment introducing [_MaybeRoundFeedBottom] claimed the
  rounded corner reveal and the comment bar paint the same token.
  Actually the corners reveal [VineTheme.navGreen] (the outer of
  [NavRoundedShell]) and the bar paints
  [VineTheme.surfaceBackground]. They happen to share the hex
  `#00150D`, which is why the seam reads as continuous — but
  "same hex" is not "same token", and the comment now says so
  explicitly so a future retune of one token doesn't silently
  invalidate the rationale.

Addresses PR #4424 review comments 3253170132 and 3253170133.

* docs(fullscreen): correct surfaceContainerHigh hex and outer-color token in _MaybeRoundFeedBottom

The body comment introducing the [NavRoundedShell] in
[_MaybeRoundFeedBottom] had three drift items:

* Claimed [VineTheme.surfaceContainerHigh] is `#1A1A1A`. The token
  is `#000A06` (see vine_theme.dart). `#1A1A1A` is
  [VineTheme.cardBackground] — a different token.
* Claimed surfaceContainerHigh is "the same neutral dark grey the
  Messages inbox uses." The Messages inbox uses cardBackground,
  not surfaceContainerHigh. The Messages-inbox association is
  residue from an earlier iteration where this code briefly used
  cardBackground; the comment was never updated when the token
  changed.
* Attributed the shell's outer color to [VineTheme.surfaceBackground]
  — same conflation as the line-870 comment fixed in a8071dd63.
  [NavRoundedShell]'s outer is [VineTheme.navGreen]; it shares its
  hex with surfaceBackground, which is what actually makes the
  seam continuous.

Corrected all three and tightened the seam claim so it depends on
the shared hex (an observable fact today) rather than on the two
tokens being the same (which they aren't).

Addresses PR #4424 review comment 3253170135.

fix(video-editor): timeline resets after clip adjustment or duplication (#4351)

* fix(timeline): ensure seekto works correctly

* fix(video-editor): make pinch zoom gap-aware to keep playhead anchored

Address review feedback on PR #4351:

- _updatePinchZoom now re-anchors through the gap-aware geometry
  helpers (timelineScrollOffsetToPosition + timelinePositionToScrollOffset)
  instead of multiplying the raw scroll offset by the pps ratio. The old
  formula over-shoots by clipsPassed * clipGap * (ratio - 1) px once the
  playhead is past clip 0, because the 1 px clip gaps don't scale with pps.
- Add _scrollOffsetToPosition wrapper symmetric to the existing
  _positionToScrollOffset helper, and route _updatePlayheadTime and
  _syncPositionFromScroll through it so all callers share one mapping.
- Add regression group in video_editor_timeline_geometry_test.dart that
  exercises the pinch path with the playhead in clip 1 and clip 2 and
  asserts the composite position stays centered after the pps change,
  plus a sanity assertion that the naive offset*ratio path drifts.

* fix(video-editor): remove trailing timeline gap at eof

* fix(video-editor): normalize timeline gap offsets

commit.message:
fix(android): default useLegacySurface to true to close FlutterJNI renderer race (#3416) (#4404)

* fix(android): default useLegacySurface to true to close FlutterJNI renderer race (#3416)

PR #3762 narrowed the ImageReaderSurfaceProducer / FlutterJNI detach
race window from "indefinite" to "1-2 in-flight frames" and explicitly
acknowledged the residual could not be closed within the SurfaceProducer
disposal path. Crashlytics issue d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a
regressed on 1.0.13 build 502 (Samsung SM-S918W, 1 fatal) — the residual
firing.

Instead of attempting an invasive synchronous MediaCodec drain, flip the
Dart-side default of useLegacySurface from false to true. The legacy
SurfaceTextureEntry backend has no ImageReader and therefore no
SDK-internal onImage callback that can run after FlutterJNI is
detached. All five accidentally-vulnerable callsites in the app
(video_editor_canvas, video_metadata_preview_screen,
video_metadata_cover_screen, video_clip_preview,
video_metadata_classic_preview_thumbnail) inherit the new default and
stop hitting the race in one change. The feed's explicit
useLegacySurface: true is unchanged; no other callsite explicitly opts
into SurfaceProducer.

The KDoc on DivineVideoPlayerInstance.enableTextureOutput is rewritten
to reflect the new default; the Kotlin function's parameter default
stays at false because Dart always passes the value over MethodChannel
(the native default is unreachable in production).

Trade-off: the five callsites lose Android 14+ SurfaceProducer
surface-recreate callbacks (Vivo/Android 16 compositor events,
permission dialogs). These flows are short-lived and don't trigger
mid-playback permission dialogs in practice; the visible failure mode
on the SurfaceProducer-recreate-needed path is a black surface until
the user navigates, which is strictly better than a fatal crash.
SurfaceProducer remains available via explicit useLegacySurface: false
when a future callsite genuinely needs it.

Out of scope (separate issues):
- media_kit_video Android backend hardening
- iOS sibling #4400 (FVP / ProVideo callback-after-teardown)
- Reflection-based MediaCodec.flush synchronous fence (rejected by
  PR #3762 as overkill; not needed once this change takes volume to zero)

* fix(android): plugin fallback uses legacy surface; document default asymmetry

Addresses review feedback on the Kotlin/Dart default mismatch in #3416.

* `DivineVideoPlayerPlugin.kt`: MethodChannel `useLegacySurface`
  fallback now `?: true` so a missing argument from Dart picks the
  safe legacy backend. Unreachable today (the controller always
  sends the value) but documents the safe-by-default intent at the
  boundary.
* `DivineVideoPlayerInstance.kt`: KDoc adds a paragraph explaining
  why the Kotlin function default stays `false` — the existing
  unit tests in `DivineVideoPlayerInstanceTest` exercise the
  `SurfaceProducer.Callback` contract via that default and would
  break if it flipped without also mocking `createSurfaceTexture()`.

Verified:
- flutter analyze (divine_video_player): clean
- flutter test (divine_video_player): 154/154 pass
- :divine_video_player:testDebugUnitTest: 22/22 pass

* fix(android): align enableTextureOutput Kotlin default with Dart and cover legacy branch (#3416)

Removes the Kotlin/Dart default asymmetry the prior commit documented.
`enableTextureOutput(..., useLegacySurface = true)` now matches the Dart
controller default and the MethodChannel fallback in
`DivineVideoPlayerPlugin`. Existing SurfaceProducer tests opt in
explicitly with `useLegacySurface = false`.

Adds two unit tests covering the now-production legacy
`SurfaceTextureEntry` branch — one asserting `createSurfaceTexture()`
is called and `createSurfaceProducer()` is not, the other pinning the
eager-attach contract on materialized players. Both use
`mockkConstructor(Surface::class)` to intercept the Android `Surface`
constructor scoped to the test that needs it.

* fix(android): align legacy texture defaults and tests

#	mobile/packages/divine_video_player/lib/src/divine_video_player_controller.dart
